dhp294:1: As the Buddhist precepts clearly forbid killing, these verses must be metaphorical; however, there is no context available to indicate exactly what each metaphor represents.
dhp302:3: _Samānasaṁvāso_ means “living together” and _dukkho_ means “suffering.” Therefore, this is a direct, unaltered translation of the Pāli: living together with others is _dukkha_.
dhp302:5: _Siyā_ means “it might be, it could be, it may be, it is possible.” Here the Buddha appears to be saying that just as it is possible to not travel, it is also possible to not suffer.
